solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mulled over anagram about alcohol

indicators.note: to mull something over is to turn it about in the mind, so these letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone puzzles over a word game while thinking about drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mulled over' is the anagram signal, though 'mulled' also hints at warmed wine, a neat false trail in a clue about drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a brandy from Gascony, a specific example of alcohol.

clue.text: Kick-off in no time?

parts.note: the moment an operation starts is reckoned as a time numbered nothing, the hour from which everything else is counted

explanation.definitionFit: The planned starting moment of a military operation is its zero hour, the kick-off of the action.

clue.text: Penny and one pioneer left out to find leader

parts.note: an ace is a playing card worth one

indicators.note: out says a letter is dropped from the word for pioneer

parts.note: a settler is a pioneer in new land

explanation.surface: A frontiersman, short of money and abandoned, goes in search of the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals the removal of 'left'; 'to find' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacesetter sets the pace for others, so is the one in the lead.

clue.text: Head of couture in tartan, being cool

indicators.note: in says the letter from couture sits inside the word for tartan

parts.note: a plaid is a tartan cloth

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fashion house's chief, dressed in tartan, stays unruffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means calm and untroubled, the temperamental sense of cool.

clue.text: Century and a half with an ancestral group

parts.note: a hundred and fifty in Roman numerals is C plus L
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family line traced back a hundred and fifty years.
explanation.walkthrough: A century is C (100) and half of it is L (50), so together CL; 'with' just joins on AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a group of families claiming descent from a common ancestor.

clue.text: Naughty gal cutting single track mixed hit

indicators.note: naughty says the letters of gal are taken in any order
cutting says those letters are cut out of the longer phrase
mixed says what is left of single track is shuffled

parts.note: the fodder from which letters are removed
the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: A naughty girl interrupting a one-line railway causes a jumbled blow.
explanation.walkthrough: Take G, A and L out of SINGLE TRACK, leaving SINETRCK, and 'mixed' rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stricken is the old past participle of strike, so it can mean hit or struck down.

clue.text: Sunniest perhaps without us turning up for the game

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word is not to be taken as it stands
without says letters of the next word are removed
turning up says the remaining letters appear in a new order

parts.note: the fodder
the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: The brightest weather, minus us, shows up for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove U and S from SUNNIEST to leave NNIEST, which 'turning up' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, a game played on a court.

clue.text: Supply eastern motor-racing team

parts.note: to equip is to supply with what is needed

explanation.surface: Providing for an oriental racing outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses a French word adopted in English motor sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Équipe is French for team, used in English for a motor-racing outfit.

clue.text: Author's alternative source

definitions.note: read as 'author is', so the definition is just the writer

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A writer's fallback place of origin.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Author's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of the writer of Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Balloonist crashing near auto

indicators.note: a crash wrecks things, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A hot-air pilot is coming down close to a car.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeronaut is a traveller in the air, especially by balloon.

clue.text: Officer Charlie meets a new islander

parts.note: a major is an army officer
Charlie is C in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: An army officer named Charlie meets a newcomer from an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Majorcan is a native of Majorca, the Balearic island.

clue.text: With crunch, credit's a guessing game

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit, with the 's as 'is' joining it on
I spy is a children's guessing game

explanation.surface: Borrowing turns out to be a game of guessing, with a crunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Crispy food is firm and brittle, breaking with a crunch.

clue.text: Well banged up, or fine?

definitions.meaning: a playful reading: being in nick (in prison, banged up) while also being good, or fine

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for prison, and 'banged up' means jailed; 'in good nick' is British for in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: In good nick is a British idiom for in fine condition or healthy.

clue.text: Force independent politician to meet the Spanish

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An unaligned MP is compelled to meet the Spaniards.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone into action, a synonym of force as a verb.

clue.text: Similar writing

explanation.definitionFit: Corresponding means both equivalent to and writing letters to someone.

clue.text: One making mummy and me present in decorated marble

indicators.note: present in says the word me is found inside the other letters
to decorate is to dress something up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone producing a mummy and me appears in ornate stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decorated' is the anagram signal and 'present in' the container; 'mummy' suggests a mother, but here it is an Egyptian corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: An embalmer preserves a corpse, as the Egyptians did when making mummies.

clue.text: Grateful to be owing money!

explanation.definitionFit: Indebted means both obliged for a kindness and literally owing money.

clue.text: Sin of excess adding to US city

parts.note: a glut is an excess
taken as written
NY is New York

explanation.surface: Wickedness of overdoing it in an American metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Sign inhibiting a violent woman

indicators.note: inhibiting means holding in, so the star sign holds the letter inside

parts.note: Virgo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A star sign holding back an aggressive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, fierce or violent woman.

clue.text: Outlaw born with sex appeal

parts.note: and joins things together like with
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A criminal blessed with charisma from birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber living outside the law, an outlaw.

clue.text: William's scruffy tuxedo concealing love letter

parts.note: Bill is the familiar form of William's name

indicators.note: scruffy means messed up, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: William's shabby dinner jacket has a romantic note tucked inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scruffy' is the anagram signal; 'concealing' only links, though it pictures the note hidden in the jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Billet-doux is French borrowed into English for a sweet note, a love letter.

clue.text: Former book about this French missile

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a book of the Bible
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: An old volume concerning a French guided weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exocet is a French-built anti-ship missile.

clue.text: Chirpy little creature having cardiac trouble, not right

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters are mixed up
not says a letter is left out of the anagram

explanation.surface: A cheerful small animal suffering heart problems that aren't quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R ('right') from CARDIAC and 'trouble' rearranges CADIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is an insect famous for its loud chirping song.

clue.text: Where a heel may come clean?

definitions.text: Where a heel may come clean?

parts.words: Where a heel may come clean?
parts.note: a heel reads like a rogue confessing, but it is the back of a foot being washed in a basin

explanation.definitionFit: A footbath is a basin for washing feet, heels and all.

clue.text: Turn up after father gets jumper

indicators.note: after places the turned piece behind the father

parts.note: FR is short for Father, a priest

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A turn-up comes along after Dad gets a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: GO ('Turn') read upwards ('up') gives OG; 'jumper' is not the sweater but a leaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog is an animal that moves by jumping.

clue.text: Frenchman turning emerald — with this?

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur

indicators.note: turning says the letters of emerald change their order

explanation.surface: A Frenchman goes green — perhaps because of this?
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' is the anagram signal; read whole, the clue describes seasickness turning a Frenchman green.
explanation.definitionFit: Mal de mer is French for seasickness, which turns a sufferer green.

clue.text: Dramatic departures

parts.note: dramatic here means on stage: the direction for several actors leaving

explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the Latin stage direction saying that characters leave the stage.

clue.text: Plain where river runs to one side

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river
right is one side, opposite left

explanation.surface: Flat country where a river flows to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthright means direct and frank, plain-speaking.
